title: The algebraic closure over a separably closed field
statement:
Let $k$ be a separably closed field
of characteristic $p$, and let $\alpha\in\bar k$ be algebraic over $k$.
Then there is an $n\ge0$ with $\alpha^{p^n}$ separable over $k$; hence
$\bar k/k$ is purely inseparable.

proof_origin.place: Fields, Lemma 9.14.6 (Tag 030K); Mathlib theorem supplies the proof

mathlib_searches.query: for an algebraic extension of a field, every element becomes separable after a p-power
algebraic closure of a separably closed field is purely inseparable
algebraic extension of a separably closed field is purely inseparable

mathlib_match.how: For the final clause, specialize the forward implication of isSepClosed_iff_isPurelyInseparable_algebraicClosure (line 558) to the algebraic closure E = k-bar, obtaining IsPurelyInseparable k E. For the first clause, apply isPurelyInseparable_iff_pow_mem (line 211) with exponential characteristic p to obtain n with alpha^(p^n) in the algebraMap range; identify that range element with k, where it is separable over k by the base-field separability instance. This is one specialization per clause; the purely-inseparable definition is Stacks Tag 09HE.
